html:
SMTO-EVT-0001 — This schedule is already running

GUID: c01ae355-e084-4f51-861f-01107347597d
Slug: event-run-conflict
Domain: EVT · Subsystem: evt

What happened

  • You asked a schedule to run now, but its previous run hasn't finished, so SMTO didn't start a second one. The run already in progress was not stopped or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Schedules, find this schedule and select Open current run. It shows whether the run is still working, waiting for your approval or waiting for your answer.
  2. If it's waiting for approval or input, respond in that run. If it's still working, wait for it to finish. A schedule can have only one run open at a time, so the earlier run must end first.
  3. If you no longer need that run, select Stop task in it. Stopping it frees the schedule; pausing or deleting the schedule does not stop a run.
  4. When the run shows Completed, Failed or Cancelled, reload Schedules and select Run now. Starting again only after the earlier run ends avoids doing the same work twice.

What success looks like

  • The schedule's button changes from Already running to Run now, and a new run starts when you select it.

If it still fails

  • If the run stays stuck as Running, select Copy error details and send them with the schedule's name to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the schedule to get around this; deleting doesn't stop the run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The event trigger was refused (409) because the scheduled event already has an open run (queued, running, awaiting_confirmation or awaiting_clarification) holding its exclusive launch slot.

What this means

  • Trigger/create_run finds an already open durable run owning the event's exclusive launch slot. Event, monitor and notification identities have separate owners. Rejected control or missing notification does not cancel an existing task; only authoritative run state establishes its outcome.

Why this can happen

  • Trigger/create_run finds an already open durable run owning the event's exclusive launch slot.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the existing event run and its authoritative state instead of creating a replacement ID.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the event's open run through the event runs route (list_agent_event_runs) or event_store.get_open_run. Let it settle, resolve its pending approval or clarification, or cancel it through the event run cancel route (cancel_agent_event_run, POST .../runs/.../cancel), then trigger again using current event state.
  • Refresh the current event/run state and use the current owner and revision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The existing run settles or is reconciled before the next supported trigger.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Event, monitor and notification identities have separate owners. Rejected control or missing notification does not cancel an existing task; only authoritative run state establishes its outcome.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
